To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a scalable RDF data store that can achieve up to a 100x speedup over existing RDF data stores when processing SPARQL queries on large RDF data sets that are partitioned across multiple nodes.

(1) the SPARQL query language is highly expressive and (2) that a scalable RDF management system that is capable of processing SPARQL queries efficiently can be built by partitioning the data in a manner that takes into account the query workload and by partitioning queries into fragments that take into account the data partitions.

(1) the SP2RDF system can be used to manage large RDF data sets on multiple machines and (2) SP2RDF is up to three-orders of magnitude more efficient at executing SPARQL queries than popular multi-node solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of efficiently querying large RDF data sets that span many machines.
the problem of how to scale RDF data management to very large data sets.
the problem of efficiently processing large-scale RDF data in a cluster environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to achieve high performance for both single node and multi-node RDF data processing.
our approach is able to scale to large datasets, and that it is up to three-orders-of-magnitude faster than the most popular multi-node RDF management systems.
our system is the first to achieve high performance RDF data management across multiple machines, and is the first system to allow the use of state-of-the-art RDF stores in a cluster environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed the first scalable RDF data management solution that allows RDF data sets to be partitioned and queried across multiple machines in a manner that is up to 100 times more efficient than popular solutions.
we introduce a scalable multi-node RDF data system that achieves high performance by taking advantage of the state-of-the-art in both single node RDF data management and parallel data processing.
we have developed the first RDF data management system to achieve high performance on both single node and multi-node deployments.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of RDF data management systems can be improved significantly by using state-of-the-art technology for single node RDF-store systems and by partitioning the data in a manner that takes advantage of the locality of RDF data.
it is possible to build a highly efficient RDF data management system for large data sets that can be partitioned across many machines.

it is possible to achieve high performance RDF data management on a cluster of machines by leveraging the state-of-the-art in single node RDF data management systems and by partitioning the data in a manner that allows the data to be processed in parallel.
